subject: geography
chapter_title: The World Population Distribution, Density and Growth

concepts.title: Patterns of Population Distribution
concepts.definition: About 90 per cent of the world's population lives on about 10 per cent of its land area, with dense clusters in East Asia, South Asia, South East Asia and Europe, where availability of water, fertile plains and mild climate attract settlement.
concepts.key_idea: Distribution is uneven because habitability is uneven: water, plains and soil pull people, deserts and tundra push them away.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy102.txt distribution patterns and factors attracting concentration

solution_steps.explain: 90 per cent of people on 10 per cent of land is the chapter's headline imbalance
East, South and South East Asia plus Europe are the four crowded regions
water availability, plains and climate explain the pull of these clusters

concepts.title: Density of Population
concepts.definition: Population density is the ratio between the number of people and the area of land they occupy, usually expressed as persons per square kilometre; the world average and country averages mask sharp internal contrasts.
concepts.key_idea: Dividing total population by land area in square kilometres yields density in persons per square kilometre.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy102.txt density definition and density of world and regions
question_patterns: define population density and give its formula
compute density when population and area are given

solution_steps.explain: density equals population divided by area in sq km

concepts.title: Population Growth and its Components
concepts.definition: Population growth is the change of population in an area between two time points, expressed as absolute change or growth rate per cent; natural growth comes from births and deaths while migration adds immigration and emigration components.
concepts.key_idea: Growth rates peak in the developing world because birth rates fall later than death rates, producing the demographic bulge.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy102.txt growth components, growth rates and demographic transition sections

solution_steps.explain: births minus deaths give natural growth; migrants give the mechanical component
growth rate per cent allows comparison across countries of different sizes
developing countries now contribute the bulk of annual additions

concepts.title: Top Ten Countries and Their Share
concepts.definition: The ten most populous countries of the world contribute about 60 per cent of the world's population, with China and India alone approaching two-fifths; the remaining world population share can be found by subtracting the top ten share from 100.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the top ten share from 100 gives the share of all other countries together.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy102.txt ten most populous countries passage (60 per cent of world population)

solution_steps.explain: the ten most populous countries hold 60 per cent of humanity

worked_examples.question_pattern: A country has a population of 24,00,000 on an area of 1,20,000 sq km. Compute its population density.

solution_template.explain: density = population / area in sq km

worked_examples.question_pattern: The ten most populous countries hold 60 per cent of world population. What is the share of all remaining countries?

solution_template.explain: 60 per cent is held by the top ten countries
100 - 60 leaves the rest of the world

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain three physical factors behind the clustering of world population.

solution_template.explain: settled life gathers around rivers, lakes and coastal water sources
flat fertile plains permit agriculture and dense rural settlement
moderate climates of Europe and monsoon Asia attract population while hot deserts and tundra repel
